description: One slide for each of the 36 default layouts, then 13 dynamic compositions (no layout record), all on one fictional six-week pilot story. The layout slides use the editorial example content of the gallery layout previews. Used to compare layouts with other designers and to review layout changes before and after.

cover.name: Cover
cover.summary: The opening slide: title, subtitle and an optional picture.
cover.description: Open a presentation with its subject and a short introduction. Add a picture when it helps establish the context.

section.name: Section
section.summary: A divider between parts: the section title and an optional subtitle.
section.description: Introduce the next part of a presentation. Use the subtitle to connect the new section to the overall argument.

agenda.name: Agenda
agenda.summary: What the talk covers: the parts, as one list that flows into columns when long.
agenda.description: Set expectations by listing the parts of a talk. Longer agendas flow across columns while preserving their order.

agenda-split.name: Agenda beside
agenda-split.summary: A concise agenda beside its title and introduction.
agenda-split.description: Introduce a concise agenda with the title and introduction on one side and the parts of the talk beside them. Use Agenda for detailed entries that need the full slide width.

statement.name: Statement
statement.description: Give one important assertion room to stand alone. Keep supporting detail on a following slide.

closing.name: Closing
closing.summary: The last slide: thanks, the call to action and contact details.
closing.description: End with the action the audience should take. Include contact details or a brief thank-you when useful.

text.name: Text
text.summary: Prose. Several blocks sit side by side when short and stack when long.
text.description: Explain one idea in continuous prose. Use paragraphs or flowing blocks for detail that needs to be read in sequence.

list.name: List
list.summary: Bulleted or numbered points; one long list flows into columns.
list.description: Present several related points in a clear sequence. Use bullets for independent points or numbered items for an ordered list.

quote.name: Quote
quote.summary: One or more quotations with attribution and photo.
quote.description: Highlight a quotation and its source. Use the attribution to explain who said it and why their perspective matters.

two-column.name: Two columns
two-column.summary: Two independent columns of any content.
two-column.description: Place two bodies of content beside each other. Use it for paired explanations or an argument with supporting evidence. Pictures remain visible in full unless an explicit fit overrides the layout default.

three-column.name: Three columns
three-column.summary: Three independent columns of any content.
three-column.description: Place three independent bodies of content beside each other. Keep equivalent comparisons parallel and use fewer columns when content needs more width. Pictures remain visible in full unless an explicit fit overrides the layout default.

pillars.name: Pillars
pillars.summary: Related ideas arranged in equal columns.
pillars.description: Show the main themes or principles behind an idea. Give each item a short heading and a comparable amount of detail.

comparison.name: Comparison
comparison.summary: Two options side by side (before and after, pros and cons, us and them), with an optional verdict.
comparison.description: Compare alternatives using parallel information. Keep the same criteria and level of detail for every option.

process.name: Process
process.summary: Steps in order, in one row.
process.description: Explain an ordered sequence of steps. Give each step a clear action and enough context to understand the transition.

timeline.name: Timeline
timeline.summary: Dated events or a roadmap along one axis, with optional notes.
timeline.description: Show events or milestones in chronological order. Label each item with a date or stage and a concise description.

faq.name: FAQ
faq.description: Answer the questions an audience is likely to ask. Pair each question with a direct answer and group related questions together.

metrics.name: Metrics
metrics.summary: One to six headline numbers, with an optional note.
metrics.description: Highlight a small set of important numbers. Give each number a label and the context needed to interpret it.

scorecard.name: Scorecard
scorecard.summary: Headline measures with their targets and status.
scorecard.description: Summarize performance across comparable measures. State the criteria consistently so the audience can assess the result.

image.name: Image
image.summary: One picture, shown whole, under an optional title.
image.description: Let one picture carry the message, shown whole at its own proportions rather than cropped. Add a short title or caption to explain what the audience should notice. For a full-bleed crop, set the image block's fit to cover.

image-beside.name: Image beside
image-beside.summary: A picture or video beside text.
image-beside.description: Explain a visual alongside its supporting text. Use the text to direct attention to the meaningful parts of the image.

gallery.name: Gallery
gallery.summary: One to six framed pictures: a screenshot, a diagram, a photo set.
gallery.description: Show several related visuals together. Use consistent captions and ordering to make the relationship between them clear.

chart.name: Chart
chart.summary: One to six charts, with an optional note.
chart.description: Give a chart enough space to show its evidence. Use the title to state the conclusion and labels to explain the measures.

chart-beside.name: Chart beside
chart-beside.summary: A chart with the takeaway beside it.
chart-beside.description: Pair a chart with an explanation of its result. Keep the text focused on the pattern or decision supported by the data.

table.name: Table
table.summary: A table across the slide, with an optional note.
table.description: Present structured data that benefits from precise comparison. Use clear row and column headings and concise cell content.

table-beside.name: Table beside
table-beside.summary: A table with commentary beside it.
table-beside.description: Place a table beside its interpretation. Use the supporting text to explain the conclusion without repeating every cell.

code.name: Code
code.summary: Source code with the explanation beside it.
code.description: Show a code example or technical excerpt. Keep the excerpt focused and use the title or caption to explain its purpose.

hero.name: Hero
hero.summary: A lead message and its supporting points beside a full-height picture.
hero.description: Combine a prominent visual or message with supporting content. Use it when one element should lead the audience into the details.

dashboard.name: Dashboard
dashboard.description: Bring several related measures and visuals into one overview. Keep labels and units consistent so the audience can scan the state quickly.

team.name: Team
team.summary: People: photo, name and role cards.
team.description: Introduce people and their roles. Use consistent names, descriptions and portraits when available.

logos.name: Logos
logos.summary: Customer, partner or sponsor logos in a grid of up to 12.
logos.description: Present organizations, partners or customers as a group. Use a consistent visual scale and add context when the relationship is not obvious.

pyramid.name: Pyramid
pyramid.summary: Levels that build on each other, as a pyramid, the first at the top.
pyramid.description: Show a hierarchy of 1 to 8 levels, from the narrow top (the peak, the few, the goal) to the broad base (the foundation, the many). Write one short list entry per level, the top level first.

matrix.name: Matrix
matrix.summary: Four parts of a whole, as the quadrants of a square beside the title.
matrix.description: Show four parts that together make a whole, or the four cases of two choices, as a 2 x 2 matrix. Write four short list entries, in the order top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right; another count is drawn as a grid of cards.

cycle.name: Cycle
cycle.summary: Steps that repeat, as a loop of nodes with arrows beside the title.
cycle.description: Show 2 to 8 steps that repeat, where the last leads back to the first (a review loop, a product lifecycle, a feedback cycle). Write one short list entry per step, in order; the first is drawn at the top and the rest clockwise, with an arrow from each to the next.

chevrons.name: Chevrons
chevrons.summary: Stages in order, as a row of chevrons.
chevrons.description: Show 1 to 8 stages that follow one another, each leading into the next. Write one short list entry per stage, in order; a word or two reads best inside a chevron.

flow.name: Flow
flow.summary: Steps in order, as boxes joined by arrows in one row.
flow.description: Show 1 to 8 steps that follow one another, each a box with an arrow to the next. Write one short list entry per step, in order.

vertical-flow.name: Vertical flow
vertical-flow.summary: Steps in order, as boxes joined by arrows in a column beside the title.
vertical-flow.description: Show 1 to 8 steps that follow one another from top to bottom, each a box with an arrow to the next, beside the title. Write one short list entry per step, in order.
